prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: العربية · المنتجات (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المنتج" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 97px
  col 2: header "السعر" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 70px
  col 3: header "المخزون" · longest unbreakable word 53px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 445px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A compact Arabic product-inventory table for scanning products, comparing prices and stock, and reading a short description as supporting detail.","reading":"Right-to-left, row by row: the reader first identifies the product on the right, then checks price and stock for comparison, and finally reads the description. The numeric columns need to align cleanly for quick vertical comparison.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 (price and stock) form a numeric comparison pair and should remain adjacent and intact.","Columns 1 and 4 (product and description) both identify the item, but the product name is the primary label and the description is secondary detail."],"keep_intact":["Price values including thousands separators and the currency marker (e.g. 3,200 ر.س)","Stock integers","Column headers","No mid-word breaks in Arabic words"],"may_wrap":["Product names at spaces","Description text at spaces"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [72, 91, 74, 122] · table 360×438px · row heights [36, 129, 60, 153, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [96, 91, 74, 98] · table 360×531px · row heights [36, 176, 60, 199, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [116, 91, 74, 78] · table 360×671px · row heights [36, 269, 60, 246, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

Only worth choosing if the reader scans descriptions more than prices; it costs the price column its clean single-line numeric rhythm."}]}
